This followed nine consecutive days with maxima of 33°C or higher amid a late-summer heatwave driven by southerly flow and Typhoon Dolphin’s lingering influence. Subsequent showers and increased cloud cover moderated conditions, preventing the extreme readings seen earlier in the month (e.g., 36.9°C on August 9). With resolution imminent and no credible upward revision to the official record expected, traders have converged on the verified 30°C threshold; only an unanticipated measurement correction or alternative station data could alter the outcome.

eventMetadata.context_description: The primary driver positioning 28°C and 29°C as the leading market-implied outcomes is the active southwest monsoon, which is forecast to deliver widespread cloud cover, scattered thunderstorms, and moderate to heavy rainfall across Metro Manila on August 18. Official PAGASA guidance and extended models indicate daily maxima near 29°C under these conditions, with high humidity and reduced solar insolation limiting daytime heating compared to clearer periods. Recent observations show similar monsoon-suppressed highs of 31°C or below amid frequent showers, consistent with August climatology where rain-cooled days typically peak in the upper 20s. Upcoming PAGASA updates and model runs will refine land-sea breeze and convective timing, key variables that could shift the exact maximum by 1–2°C.
